title_or_table: Medicaid and CHIP renewals, April 2023 to March 2024: nested funnel stages from one base
table_id: data.medicaid.gov dataset e6205a51-e6d7-4849-9882-4483b8a28c41, October 2024 release, metrics 5 to 5d
observation_period: Renewals due April 2023 to March 2024 (twelve reporting months)
geography: United States, the sum of the states’ reports (checked equal by script)
universe_or_base: Beneficiaries due for renewal in the twelve months; each stage sits inside the one before
unit: people; share_of_due is the stage over renewals due, computed and stored to four decimals
vintage: Updated renewal outcomes, October 2024 final release (dataset modified November 1, 2024)
qualification: State-reported counts, "updated" to show renewals that were pending three months after they were due; states began the unwinding in different months (4 reported renewals due in March 2023, and all 50 states and DC from July 2023), and the file ends with renewals due in March 2024, before the unwinding ended in every state. A person due in two months of the file counts twice. Pending renewals are set apart, not counted as decided. The figures differ from V7 I062’s "more than 25 million" disenrolled (KFF, through 2024), because this file ends with March 2024 renewals.

stage.description: stage label, plain words for the table

people.description: people at this stage, summed over the twelve months

role.description: stage (a nested funnel step), set apart (pending), drop (a way out between stages) or split (a breakdown of kept)

printed_source_line: Source: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Medicaid and CHIP Updated Renewal Outcomes, renewals due April 2023 to March 2024, United States. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Stages summed by Oath & Action from the national rows; pending renewals set apart.
domain_note: V7 files paperwork that pushes people off benefits under Congress, agencies and public services (I062, "Delivering services")
derivation: Sums of the national monthly rows for April 2023 to March 2024; decided is due less pending, not ended for a procedural reason is decided less procedural endings, kept is renewed (5a); the script asserts the stages nest.
notes: Ended in the twelve months: 22,914,537, of whom 15,966,431 (69.7 percent) for a procedural reason.
V7 I062 (observed 2024-09) cites KFF: more than 25 million disenrolled, 69 percent for procedural reasons; the chart prints CMS’s own figures and period (data lead change 11).

Procedural reason, in CMS’s words (read November 13, 2026): its file names metric 5c “Total beneficiaries whose coverage was terminated for a procedural or administrative reason”, beside metric 5b, “Total beneficiaries determined ineligible for Medicaid and CHIP based on the return of a renewal form”. The description of CMS’s original renewal data (Medicaid and CHIP CAA Reporting Metrics, data.medicaid.gov) adds: “States that held procedural terminations reflect these data in metric 5d as pending renewals along with renewals that were due but not completed by the end of the reporting period.” The file, its data dictionary and both datasets’ descriptions give no examples of a procedural reason; CMS’s Data Sources and Metrics Definitions Overview, on medicaid.gov, refused this container (HTTP 403) and was not read.

What a procedural ending is, in the rules’ words (BC-S9, read November 13, 2026). The renewal rule in force through the file’s period, 42 CFR 435.916(a)(3)(iii) (77 FR 17210, March 23, 2012; eCFR as of October 1, 2023), tells the state to “Reconsider in a timely manner the eligibility of an individual who is terminated for failure to submit the renewal form or necessary information, if the individual subsequently submits the renewal form within 90 days after the date of termination”. CMS’s 2024 eligibility rule (89 FR 22780, April 2, 2024) speaks of “individuals who are terminated for procedural reasons (that is, because they did not respond to the State’s request for additional information)” (at 22800) and of “losing coverage due to procedural reasons, including, for example, failure to return paperwork” (at 22781). Section 1902(tt)(1) of the Social Security Act, under which states reported these counts, names the two kinds apart: those terminated and, of them, those terminated “for procedural reasons”. No record read says how many people ended for a procedural reason were still eligible, or which reason was most common.
